summary.body:
This is a comment-only change to `last_n` and matches its stated intent: no behavior change, just documenting what happens when `n` exceeds `len(items)`.

Verified the claim against the actual slice semantics: `items[-n:]` when `n > len(items)` does return the whole list, because the negative start index clips to 0 rather than wrapping or erroring. The new comment is accurate for the case it describes.

(Aside, not a defect in this diff: `items[-n:]` also returns the whole list when `n == 0`, since `-0 == 0` and `items[0:]` is the full list, which some readers might not expect from a function named `last_n`. The comment doesn't claim to cover that case, and the diff isn't changing behavior, so I'm not flagging it as an issue here — just noting it in case a follow-up wants to document or guard it.)

No material defect found; approving as-is.
